purpose: Teach: ６つ/ミソ/外野/ヤミ/タネ/キズ/オジサン/くず

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが子供達を６つの組に分けて指導された
lines.en: When you were young, your father would divide the children into six groups and teach them.
lines.style: Soft opening, as if retrieving a half-remembered scene. Gentle, almost dreamy pacing. Slight breathiness—the voice of someone speaking to the past as much as the present.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、ミソ作りを習われたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes—and your grandfather taught you miso-making, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Warm, affirming tone. Light lift on the question mark. A smile in the voice—the comfort of shared memory confirmed. Gentle, unhurried.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが「外野席で野球を観た」と語られた
lines.en: Your father used to talk about watching baseball from the outfield bleachers when you were young.
lines.style: Same wistful opening. Slightly longer pause before the specific memory. Voice settles into it like settling into a photograph. Trailing softly.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、戦後のヤミ市場をご存知だったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And your grandfather knew about the black markets after the war, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Same warm baseline. Light knowing in the tone—she's following his thread. Not a question that needs answering, but an invitation to remember together.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが野菜のタネを蒔かれた
lines.en: When you were young, your father would plant vegetable seeds.
lines.style: Quieter this time, almost reverent. Slower pace. The simplicity of the act seems to matter—voice lingers gently on 'plant.' Trailing off into stillness.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、戦争の心のキズを抱えて来られたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And your grandfather carried the wounds of war in his heart all these years, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Tender, but with weight beneath. Not heavy—careful. A pause before speaking, as if honoring what that meant. Voice stays steady and close, like she's saying something she's thought about for a long time.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは皆から「オジサン」と慕われた
lines.en: When you were young, everyone looked up to your father like an older brother.
lines.style: Same wistful opening. Warmth creeping in—pride in this memory. Slight lift in the middle. Trailing with affection and gentle sadness that the era has passed.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、終戦直後、くず米でも有り難く頂いたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: After the war ended, your grandfather was grateful even for the broken rice, wasn't he, dear?
lines.style: Close and intimate, almost whispered. Deep gratitude in every word. A long, knowing pause before 'dear'—she's making sure he understands she knows what that meant. Voice settles at the end with quiet reverence.
